result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.directed_steiner_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find an approximate directed Steiner tree (Steiner arborescence). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L28197-L28288){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.directed_steiner_tree( root, terminal_nodes, weight_attr=None, return_subgraph=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Directed Steiner tree](/assets/graphs/directed-steiner-tree.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A directed version of the steiner_tree graph, rooted at B with terminals C and E outlined. The edge between C and D now points from C to D, so C cannot be reached through D: the arborescence B→D→E→C (accent) reaches E through the non-terminal D and then C from E. The card lists the three edges and their total weight 2 + 1 + 4 = 7." width="100%"} Given a root node and a set of terminal nodes, finds an approximate minimum-weight arborescence rooted at `root` containing a directed path from `root` to every terminal. Uses the Shortest-Path Heuristic (SPH) with edge-cost reuse: greedily selects the cheapest path from root to an uncovered terminal, then zeroes the cost of used edges so future paths reuse them for free. This encourages path sharing and produces compact arborescences. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [root]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Label of the root (source) node. [terminal_nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Labels of the target nodes that must be reachable from `root`. [weight_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge attribute to use for weights. If `None`, uses the default `weight` field (or `1.0` if unweighted). [return_subgraph]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), return a new directed `Graph` containing only the arborescence edges. If `False`, return the raw edge list. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph | list[tuple[str, str, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_subgraph=True`: a new directed `Graph` with the arborescence. Otherwise a list of `(source, target, weight)` tuples. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is not directed, a node is not found, or a terminal is not reachable from root. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A simple directed tree where the root fans out to several targets: ::: {#9b30884d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) for n in ["R", "A", "B", "C", "D"]: g.add_node(label=n) g.add_edge("R", "A", weight=1.0) g.add_edge("A", "B", weight=2.0) g.add_edge("R", "C", weight=5.0) g.add_edge("A", "C", weight=1.0) g.add_edge("C", "D", weight=1.0) tree = g.directed_steiner_tree("R", ["B", "D"]) tree.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 4 ``` ::: :::
